title: GsimSimResultDocument
description: A .gsim_sim_result: the metadata of one simulation run — what it was, which signals it holds with their units and quantities, and how they were laid out — plus where the samples live. They can be inline in this file, or in an HDF5 file it points at.

schema_version.description: Readers reject any other value rather than guessing. A v1 document (samples always inline) is upgraded to this shape before validation, so files already written stay readable.

id.description: The sim id this run had in the kernel. Not a key into anything after the fact — the file is self-contained — but it ties a result back to a log line.

source.description: Workspace-relative path of the .gsim_sch this came from, when it came from one.

created.description: ISO-8601 timestamp. Not declared as `format: date-time`: the validators are compiled in ajv strict mode without ajv-formats, where an unknown format is an error rather than a hint.

engine.description: Engine build that produced it, so a result can be reproduced.

sweep.description: The shared x axis. Every signal is sampled at these points, in this order.

layout.description: How the viewer had these signals arranged. Optional: a file without it opens with one axes per quantity.

signals.description: Signal names, resolved against `signals` by name.

colors.description: Per-signal trace colour, positionally. Absent means the viewer's default palette.

kind.description: inline: every vector carries its own `encoding` and `data`, and the file stands alone — it can be committed, attached to a review or emailed. hdf5: the samples, and the LOD pyramid over them, live in the file `path` points at, and each vector names its `dataset`.

path.description: Required when kind is hdf5. Relative to this file's directory, so a result and its data move together.

pyramid.description: Whether the HDF5 file carries precomputed LOD levels. A reader that knows there are none can skip looking for them.

encoding.description: f64-base64 is base64 of little-endian IEEE-754 doubles: exact, and about half the size of decimal text. json is a plain array of numbers, for a small result someone wants to read or diff.

domain.description: Decides the x-axis name and whether it is logarithmic.

encoding.description: Required when data.kind is inline. f64-base64 is base64 of little-endian IEEE-754 doubles: exact, and about half the size of decimal text. json is a plain array of numbers, for a small result someone wants to read or diff.

dataset.description: Required when data.kind is hdf5: the dataset key inside the HDF5 file (`<block_id>__<port_id>`).

quantity.description: voltage, current, power, dB, deg, … It groups signals onto a shared y-axis, so two signals with the same quantity share a scale.

analysis.description: tran, ac_mag, ac_phase, … ac_mag/ac_phase put the viewer in Bode mode.

encoding.description: Required when data.kind is inline. f64-base64 is base64 of little-endian IEEE-754 doubles: exact, and about half the size of decimal text. json is a plain array of numbers, for a small result someone wants to read or diff.

dataset.description: Required when data.kind is hdf5: the dataset key inside the HDF5 file (`<block_id>__<port_id>`).
